\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{درخواست} \fa{کردن} (darkhâst kardan)}{درخواست کردن (darkhâst kardan)}]{\fa{درخواست} \fa{کردن} (darkhâst kardan) — to request, to ask for (formally)}

\label{lesson:FA-C441-darkhast-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for smelly, then the Persian for a water heater.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{درخواست} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{درخواست} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{darkhâst kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to request, to ask for (formally)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{از} \fa{مدیر} \fa{هتل} \fa{یک} \fa{اتاق} \fa{دیگر} \fa{درخواست} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Az modir-e hotel yek otâq-e digar darkhâst kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We asked the hotel manager for another room.
\end{quote}

\emph{darkhâst} 'a request' + \emph{kardan}. The person asked takes \emph{az}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{darkhâst kardan} is built from \emph{darkhâst} 'a request', which EtymDB lists and which is built on \emph{khâstan} 'to want', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darkhâst kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{darkhâst kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{darkhâst kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for smelly, then the Persian for a water heater, then say \emph{darkhâst kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رسیدگی} \fa{کردن} (residegi kardan)}{رسیدگی کردن (residegi kardan)}]{\fa{رسیدگی} \fa{کردن} (residegi kardan) — to look into, to deal with (a problem)}

\label{lesson:FA-C441-residegi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a water heater, then the Persian for to request.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رسیدگی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{رسیدگی} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{residegi kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to look into, to deal with (a problem)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مدیر} \fa{قول} \fa{داد} \fa{به} \fa{مشکل} \fa{ما} \fa{رسیدگی} \fa{کند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Modir qol dâd be moshkel-e mâ residegi konad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager promised to look into our problem.
\end{quote}

\emph{residegi} 'attention, follow-up', from \emph{residan}. The matter takes \emph{be}: \emph{be in kâr residegi mikonim}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{residegi kardan} is built from \emph{residegi} 'attending to', formed on \emph{residan} 'to arrive, to reach', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{rasīdan}, and \emph{kardan} 'to do'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{residegi kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{residegi kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a water heater, then the Persian for to request, then say \emph{residegi kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ایراد} \fa{گرفتن} (irâd gereftan)}{ایراد گرفتن (irâd gereftan)}]{\fa{ایراد} \fa{گرفتن} (irâd gereftan) — to find fault, to pick holes}

\label{lesson:FA-C441-irad-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to request, then the Persian for to look into.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ایراد} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{ایراد} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{irâd gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to find fault, to pick holes\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{از} \fa{همه} \fa{چیز} \fa{هتل} \fa{ایراد} \fa{میگرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U az hame chiz-e hotel irâd migereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He found fault with everything about the hotel.
\end{quote}

\emph{irâd} 'objection, fault' + \emph{gereftan}. The thing criticized takes \emph{az}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{irâd gereftan} is built from \emph{irâd} 'an objection, a flaw', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{īrād} 'bringing forward', and the native verb \emph{gereftan} 'to take'. EtymDB does not list \emph{irâd}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{irâd gereftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{irâd gereftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to request, then the Persian for to look into, then say \emph{irâd gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کوتاه} \fa{آمدن} (kutâh âmadan)}{کوتاه آمدن (kutâh âmadan)}]{\fa{کوتاه} \fa{آمدن} (kutâh âmadan) — to back down, to give in}

\label{lesson:FA-C441-kutah-amadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to look into, then the Persian for to find fault.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کوتاه} \fa{آمدن}}
\textbf{\fa{کوتاه} \fa{آمدن}} (\emph{kutâh âmadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to back down, to give in\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مسافر} \fa{عصبانی} \fa{بود} \fa{ولی} \fa{آخر} \fa{کوتاه} \fa{آمد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mosâfer 'asabâni bud vali âkhar kutâh âmad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The passenger was angry but in the end he backed down.
\end{quote}

Literally 'to come short'. Present: \emph{kutâh miâyad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kutâh âmadan} is built from native \emph{kutâh} 'short', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{kōtāh}, and \emph{âmadan} 'to come', which EtymDB traces to the PIE root \emph{g\textsuperscript{w}em-}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to look into, then the Persian for to find fault, then say \emph{kutâh âmadan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ناراضی} (nârâzi)}{ناراضی (nârâzi)}]{\fa{ناراضی} (nârâzi) — dissatisfied, unhappy (with something)}

\label{lesson:FA-C441-narazi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to find fault, then the Persian for to back down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ناراضی}}
\textbf{\fa{ناراضی}} (\emph{nârâzi}) — \textquotedblleft{}dissatisfied, unhappy (with something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مشتریها} \fa{از} \fa{غذای} \fa{رستوران} \fa{ناراضی} \fa{بودند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Moshtari-hâ az ghazâ-ye restorân nârâzi budand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The customers were unhappy with the restaurant's food.
\end{quote}

\emph{nâ-} 'not' + \emph{râzi} 'satisfied'. The cause takes \emph{az}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nârâzi} is built from the native prefix \emph{nâ-} 'not' and \emph{râzi} 'satisfied', borrowed from Arabic \emph{rāḍī} 'content, pleased' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
